unit.title: Linear Systems as a Tested Software Component
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building practical software-engineering skill

included: solution sets of square linear systems
input contracts and explicit failure modes
deterministic unit tests and residual-based checks
excluded: a claim of coverage of MIT 18.06
a claim of textbook or lecture completion
matrix factorization libraries beyond the assigned solver
any normalized catalog record not yet verified as an instructional unit

learning_objectives: Connect row operations, pivots, and solution-set classification.
Specify a small linear-system solver with observable, testable behavior.
Implement elimination and back substitution without delegating the core algorithm to a numerical library.
Use partial pivoting and a documented scale-aware tolerance policy.
Build deterministic tests for normal, adversarial, and invalid inputs.
Explain the difference between algorithmic correctness, a small residual, and production numerical reliability.

unit_complete_when: All requested submission artifacts exist in the later learner attempt workspace.
Harness-controlled deterministic checks pass the solver contract and isolation requirements.
An examiner applies the independent rubric to the captured artifacts and evidence.
The resulting durable job transition is accepted by the control plane.
completion_policy.after_unit_completion: Keep the course IN_PROGRESS; this kickoff establishes only one bounded foundation.
completion_policy.whole_course_completion: Requires separately prepared and validated later units covering a declared course-wide outcome set; no such completion is claimed by this package.

provenance.authorship_note: The kickoff sequence and software task are new course-manager work. They are not represented as an official MIT unit, a Gilbert Strang text excerpt, or a 3Blue1Brown lesson.
